title: Zero Trust: never trust, always verify

videos.script: Every rule so far has trusted a packet partly because of where it came from. The staff network may use the application, because it is the staff network. {{where}} Zero Trust removes that reason. Every request has to prove who is making it, wherever it arrives from. {{who}} In this lesson the application gets a front door that asks for a certificate. A laptop inside the office, allowed through by the firewall, is refused at that door. {{refused}} The proxy gets an identity of its own, and both ends of their connection prove who they are. {{mtls}} Every request is written down with the identity that made it. And an expired certificate is refused on the spot, with nobody having to revoke anything. {{expired}}
